subject.title: [Feature] Decouple dreaming from memory-core — allow any memory plugin to implement dreaming protocol

question: Should OpenClaw expose an OpenClaw-managed dreaming plugin protocol, or should dreaming orchestration remain owned by individual memory plugins on ClawHub?
rationale: Current seams allow a memory plugin to expose a dreaming config block and allow ClawHub plugins to implement their own pipeline, but they do not expose a public lifecycle protocol for OpenClaw to orchestrate third-party storage backends. Choosing that boundary creates public SDK/config/runtime surface and should be coordinated with the memory role-slot direction.

options.title: Design a narrow core protocol
options.body: Define a maintainer-approved SDK/runtime contract for query, promote, and state-reporting hooks after the memory role-slot taxonomy settles.

options.title: Keep dreaming plugin-owned
options.body: Close this direction after documenting that memory plugins should ship their own dreaming pipeline through ClawHub instead of core orchestration.

options.title: Wait for role-slot landing
options.body: Leave this issue open but block implementation until the broader memory role-slot PR is merged, narrowed, or closed.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow core protocol
recommendation.body: Define a maintainer-approved SDK/runtime contract for query, promote, and state-reporting hooks after the memory role-slot taxonomy settles.

likelyOwner.reason: vignesh07 introduced the memory-core dreaming feature and is the strongest history-backed routing candidate for the dreaming lifecycle boundary.
